outcome.answer:
Yes. A paper by Benjamin Tannenbaum directly studies the conversation-context effect on AI answers and finds that using the full prior conversation versus only the final user message changes answers materially in 44.7% of cases; full-conversation answers also score higher on request satisfaction [1]. Adding a short reconstructed prefix reduces, but does not eliminate, the effect: materially different answers still remain in almost one third of cases, so compressed context is not equivalent to full dialogue history [1].

A related Tannenbaum paper explains why this happens: the final prompt often contains only part of the conversation-conditioned request state, and important request dimensions are often present in earlier turns but missing from the last message [2]. That paper measures how request state is distributed across turns, while the first paper estimates the causal effect of omitted same-conversation history on answer quality and content [1,2].
